review.content_class_rationale: Supplementary Video S1: clinic and hallway video of the index patient with DBS off and on (gait, arm posture and spiral drawing tasks), cited in the case text.

ownership_evidence.quote: Supplementary Video S1 reveals video collected with DBS turned off and on

review.notes: Viewed 13 sampled full-resolution frames (every 5 s from 0 to 60 s). Frames show a black opening frame, a seated man with outstretched arms in an examination room, a close view of a spiral/handwriting task on a table with a pencil, hallway walking toward and away from the camera with one hand on the wall, a full-screen "DBS ON" title card, and a later repeat of the room, drawing and hallway scenes, plus a scene with a standing woman in red (a second person or examiner) gesturing and a man in a gray top in the room and hallway. Faces are covered with blur or mosaic bars in the patient scenes, but the coverage is incomplete in places (see limitations).
limitations: Frames sampled every 5 s from 0 to 60 s (13 frames); frames between samples, the final 5 s, continuous motion and audio were not reviewed.
A "DBS ON" title card was seen at 20 s; a matching DBS OFF card was not among the sampled frames, so which segments are DBS off versus on was not confirmed from the sampled frames.
Scenes are not dated or labeled with a visit time; the last scenes show different clothing and a second person, and the source does not state which visit each scene belongs to.

Privacy (categories only): at 50 s a non-patient examiner (second person, a woman) has her face visible in unblurred profile (face_or_identifiable_person); at 45 s the patient mosaic bar is offset, leaving part of the head and upper face visible (face_or_identifiable_person); at 50 s the patient lower face shows below the bar (face_or_identifiable_person); at 5 s and 30 s documents on the wall carry an institution logo (direct_identifiers); in the hallway scenes room-number signs are visible (direct_identifiers).
The second person in the later scenes is described only as a second person or examiner; her role was not stated in the source and is not inferred.
No clinical facts were taken from the video; facts come from the text only.
